solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Working lunches with a macabre sort of lawyer

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked over and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A grim kind of solicitor talks business over lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges LUNCHES plus A MACABRE; 'with' just joins the two parts of the fodder. An ambulance chaser is a lawyer who touts for accident-injury claims.
explanation.definitionFit: A derogatory name for an attorney who pursues accident victims for compensation cases.

clue.text: Lose oar at sea in spray

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rower drops an oar overboard amid the spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges LOSE OAR; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressurised can that releases a fine mist is the everyday sense of spray here.

clue.text: A gem of a girl?

definitions.meaning: a precious stone, usually green or blue

explanation.walkthrough: The precious stone and a woman's name share one spelling; the question mark flags the play on 'a gem of a girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mineral is a valued stone and also a traditional female forename.

clue.text: Built with care abroad to minimise friction

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Something was carefully constructed overseas to run smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges BUILT and CARE; 'with' joins them and 'to' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying oil or grease to moving parts is done precisely to reduce rubbing resistance.

clue.text: Hazel, for example, one who's crazy over old actor

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written over another comes above it

parts.note: a nut is slang for a madman
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A mad fan towers over a veteran thespian called Hazel.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel looks like a woman's name but is a shrub bearing cobnuts. Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated London stage actor around 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: The hazel bears edible cobnuts, making it one example of a nut-bearing plant.

clue.text: A country seat? No, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dodgy or not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a rural estate and voices doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A country seat' reads as a stately home, but 'A country' is the definition; 'suspect' rearranges SEAT NO I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baltic republic in northern Europe, bordering Latvia and Russia.

clue.text: Chase round a resort

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the next one

parts.note: to chase is to hunt

explanation.surface: Someone pursues a target around a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts A inside HUNT. 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is a place one frequents.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite spot visited often is a regular resort or stamping ground.

clue.text: Comic-strip character, perhaps getting petrol on her overalls initially

parts.note: super is the British name for high-octane four-star petrol
taken as written

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure's overalls get splashed with fuel at the pump.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPER was the British name for top-grade petrol; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Caped crime-fighters with powers are typical characters in comic books.

clue.text: Train always holding one up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
holding means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever
a unit is a single thing

explanation.surface: A train that always carries one passenger upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' builds EUNITER and 'up' turns the whole thing round. 'Train' looks like a railway but means a group of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: The attendants following a monarch form a train, a body of retainers.

clue.text: Seldom encountered by British, Italian cheese dish

indicators.note: by means set next to the following pieces

parts.note: something rare is seldom met with
It is a short form of Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: An unusual cheese dish turns up in Britain and Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rarebit is Welsh rarebit, melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a savoury of seasoned melted cheese served on toast.

clue.text: Mutter curiously about piano and something to play

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
curiously means in an odd way, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone mumbles oddly about the piano and their instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges MUTTER into TRUMET, and 'about' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument is played by blowing, so it is a thing one plays.

clue.text: Trooper willing to keep going

parts.note: a trooper is a soldier
on means willing, as in I'm on for it

explanation.surface: A dedicated trooper is willing to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' for willing is as in 'are you on for it?'; 'to' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere doggedly despite difficulty, as a soldier presses forward.

clue.text: Go round one Italian city

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the next

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in your turn
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller circles an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts I inside TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Piedmont in northern Italy, home of the famous Shroud.

clue.text: Escape of water from a lake, unfortunately, by outskirts of Grasmere

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters are rearranged
outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Water is draining from a Lake District lake near Grasmere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges A LAKE into LEAKA, and 'outskirts of' gives GE. Grasmere is a village in England's Lake District; 'from' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A seepage or loss of liquid through a hole or crack.

clue.text: Complete change of opinion concerning female expert

parts.note: about means concerning
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A woman specialist makes a dramatic U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a military turn to face the other way, figuratively a total reversal of stance.

clue.text: A grant secured by the Olympian

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: An Olympic competitor receives a sports grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured by' builds THLETE. 'Olympian' sounds like a Greek god but means a Games competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in the Olympic Games is a sportsperson, typically in track and field.

clue.text: Charm of Arab, say, connected with Oxford?

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
an Oxford is a type of laced shoe

explanation.surface: A lucky token involves an Arab and a link to the university town.
explanation.walkthrough: Arab and Oxford seem to be about people and places: one is a horse breed, the other a style of shoe. 'connected with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped iron is traditionally hung up as a lucky token or talisman.

clue.text: Saying name of dog, perhaps held by lead

indicators.note: held by means the piece goes inside the next one

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover is a stock name for a pet dog

explanation.surface: The command to a dog is given while it is kept on its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' suggests a dog leash but is the metal, chemical symbol Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a traditional short saying expressing a general truth.

clue.text: Rustic worker after vegetables

indicators.note: after means the worker piece comes after the vegetables

parts.note: peas are vegetables
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A farmhand is out chasing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A country labourer of humble standing, especially a smallholder working the land.

clue.text: Fish lake wearing straw hat

indicators.note: the hat is worn around the other piece, so it contains it

parts.note: a boater is a flat-topped straw hat

explanation.surface: A fish from the lake sports a straw hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a stiff straw hat with a flat crown, as worn for punting.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoked whole herring is a kipper-like fish, cured but not split.

clue.text: Significance of less than wholesome wine

indicators.note: less than means a letter short, so the end is cut off

parts.note: pure means clean and wholesome
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: What does it mean that this wine is not quite healthy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' drops the last letter of PURE to give PUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The purport of a document is its gist or meaning.

clue.text: Gradually disappear in route through mountains on holiday

parts.note: a pass is a way through mountains
off means away from work, on leave

explanation.surface: Someone fades away while trekking through the mountains on vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade away or subside little by little, as a feeling or symptom does.

clue.text: Youngster in Po Delta, swimming?

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young creature is swimming in the mouth of Italy's river Po.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges PO DELTA; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the young larval stage of a frog or toad.

clue.text: Change flag once fellow leaves

indicators.note: leaves means the named letter goes away

parts.note: to flag is to tire or falter

explanation.surface: A banner is changed once a man departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is a verb meaning to weaken; 'once' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify or change it.

clue.text: Piece of music from wassailer on doorstep

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Christmas carollers on the doorstep perform a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: A wassailer is a carol singer going door to door.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form whose main theme recurs between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Main place for the rest of the natives?

definitions.text: Main place for the rest of the natives?

parts.words: Main place for the rest of the natives?
parts.note: main is the sea, natives are oysters raised in British waters, and the rest is where they sleep

explanation.surface: Where do locals of the mainland go for a nap?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea and 'natives' are a crossword name for native British oysters; 'rest' plays on lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellfish farming area on the seabed where molluscs are bred.

clue.text: Little time in Indonesian island for a British-style type of curry

indicators.note: in means the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: Bali is an island of Indonesia
t is a small abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Briefly on an Indonesian island, someone orders a curry in the British style.
explanation.walkthrough: Balti curry was developed in Birmingham, England; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balti is a spicy dish cooked and served in a wok-like pan, popularised in Birmingham.

clue.text: In conflict with commander this month

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman military commander
inst., instant, means of this month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A commanding officer is at odds this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) was formal letter-writing shorthand for 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposed to or in opposition to someone or something.

clue.text: Put rings round the lines for play's hero

indicators.note: round means the rings go around the other pieces

parts.note: o is a ring shape, so two rings give two Os
taken as written
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: An actor surrounds the script with circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link; 'round' places the two Os on either side. The hero is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moor of Venice is the title role in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Play's hero overcome? Not he, if composed

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: The tragic lead is beaten, but this one is not, if he stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges OVERCOME, NOT, HE, IF. The title is the full subtitle of Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: The full title of Shakespeare's play is Othello, The Moor of Venice, naming its protagonist.
